in_arabic.name: دولة
in_arabic.meaning: دولة تعني الدولة أو الحكم أو السلطة في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: دولة هي كلمة عربية تعني الدولة أو الحكم أو السلطة، وتأتي من الجذر 'دول' الذي يعني 'يدول' أي يتحول أو يتغير، ومن ثم فهي تشير إلى التغيير أو التحول في الحكم أو السلطة، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران آية ١٠٤ {وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ وَأُولَـئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ} حيث تشير إلى الأمة التي تدعو إلى الخير وتحكم بالعدل

in_english.name: Daulah
in_english.meaning: Daulah means state, government, or authority in English
in_english.long_meaning: The name Daulah is derived from the Arabic root 'd-w-l' which means 'to change' or 'to turn', and it refers to the concept of state, government, or authority. This term has significant importance in Islamic tradition, as mentioned in the Quran, Surah Al Imran, verse 104, where it refers to a community that calls to good and enjoins justice. Historically, the term has been used to signify the transition or change in power or governance. In modern usage, Daulah symbolizes good governance, justice, and moral leadership

data.cultural_impact: The name "Daulah" holds significant cultural importance in Islamic history, particularly during the era of the Islamic golden age when caliphates and empires reigned supreme. It signifies a leader or a ruler who has the power and authority to govern and manage the state's affairs effectively and justly. The name is still prevalent in Muslim communities, particularly among those with a political or aristocratic background.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Daulah" represents the divine guidance and leadership of Allah. It reminds us that true power and authority come from Allah and that those who rule justly and with the fear of Allah are considered His vicegerents on Earth. The name also highlights the responsibility of individuals to submit to Allah's will and follow the guidance of righteous leaders. Overall, the name "Daulah" is a reminder of the interconnectedness of religion and politics, and the importance of just governance and leadership in creating a harmonious and peaceful society.
